column1: Start a protected T-SQL block with {{c1::BEGIN TRY}}.
column2:
Close the protected statements with END TRY.
Review source

column1: END TRY must be followed immediately by {{c1::BEGIN CATCH}}.
column2:
No intervening statements are allowed.
Review source

column1: A TRY...CATCH construct must remain within one {{c1::batch}}.
column2:
Do not put GO between its TRY and CATCH blocks.
Review source

column1: Within CATCH, {{c1::ERROR_NUMBER()}} returns the caught error's numeric identifier.
column2:
This identifies the error rather than its severity or state.
Review source

column1: Within CATCH, {{c1::ERROR_MESSAGE()}} returns the complete error message text.
column2:
The text includes substituted values such as object names.
Review source

column1: Within CATCH, {{c1::ERROR_SEVERITY()}} returns the caught error's severity level.
column2:
Severity is distinct from the user-defined state value.
Review source

column1: Within CATCH, {{c1::ERROR_STATE()}} returns the caught error's state number.
column2:
A state value can help identify where an error was raised.
Review source

column1: Within CATCH, {{c1::ERROR_LINE()}} returns the line where the error occurred.
column2:
This identifies the error's location rather than the logging statement's location.
Review source

column1: Within CATCH, {{c1::ERROR_PROCEDURE()}} returns the name of the stored procedure or trigger where the error originated.
column2:
It identifies the origin rather than merely the procedure doing the logging.
Review source

column1: Outside the scope of any CATCH, the ERROR_* information functions return {{c1::NULL}}.
column2:
Their values depend on an active caught-error context.
Review source

column1: Inside CATCH, rethrow the caught exception with {{c1::THROW;}}.
column2:
The parameterless form preserves the original exception.
Review source

column1: If a caught error has severity 14, bare THROW; rethrows it with severity {{c1::14}}.
column2:
A bare rethrow preserves the caught exception's severity.
Review source

column1: A newly numbered THROW requires an error number of at least {{c1::50000}}.
column2:
This minimum does not restrict a parameterless rethrow of an existing system error.
Review source

column1: THROW accepts state values from {{c1::0 to 255}}.
column2:
Zero is valid, despite the training unit's stated lower bound of one.
Review source

column1: A THROW that initiates a new exception sets severity to {{c1::16}}.
column2:
There is no severity argument in THROW's parameter list.
Review source

column1: In THROW 50001, N'Invalid quantity.', 7; the 7 is the {{c1::state}}.
column2:
It can distinguish this raise site from another using the same error number.
Review source

column1: The statement immediately before THROW must end with {{c1::a semicolon (;)}}.
column2:
Terminate the preceding statement before raising or rethrowing the exception.
Review source

column1: For new T-SQL error-raising code, Microsoft recommends {{c1::THROW}}.
column2:
It honors XACT_ABORT, unlike RAISERROR.
Review source

column1: In a RAISERROR message, %s substitutes a {{c1::string}}.
column2:
Supply the replacement value after the severity and state arguments.
Review source

column1: In a RAISERROR message, %d formats a {{c1::signed integer}}.
column2:
Supply an INT value as its substitution argument.
Review source

column1: Enable automatic transaction abort for applicable run-time errors with SET {{c1::XACT_ABORT}} ON;
column2:
Compile errors are outside this option, and RAISERROR does not honor it.
Review source

column1: XACT_STATE() = {{c1::0}} means there is no active user transaction.
column2:
There is no transaction to commit or roll back.
Review source

column1: XACT_STATE() = {{c1::1}} means the active user transaction is committable.
column2:
Committability does not prove that the business operation succeeded.
Review source

column1: XACT_STATE() = {{c1::-1}} means the active user transaction cannot be committed.
column2:
A full rollback is required before ordinary writes can resume.
Review source

column1: Start an explicit transaction with {{c1::BEGIN TRANSACTION}};
column2:
This groups the following work under transaction control.
Review source

column1: For a transaction your procedure owns, IF {{c1::@@TRANCOUNT}} > 0 ROLLBACK TRANSACTION; avoids rollback when none is active.
column2:
The guard detects presence rather than whether a transaction is committable.
Review source

column1: A successful COMMIT TRANSACTION changes @@TRANCOUNT from 2 to {{c1::1}}.
column2:
An inner COMMIT does not finish the outer transaction.
Review source

column1: In RAISERROR(N'Invalid quantity.', 16, 1), 16 is the {{c1::severity}}.
column2:
Severity 16 transfers control to CATCH when raised inside TRY.
Review source
